title: She asked me where I lived
wm: Direct and Indirect Speech: Questions and Commands
intro: Reported questions use statement order and no question mark: She asked me where I lived. Yes/no questions use “if” or “whether”. Requests and orders use ask/tell + person + to + verb: He asked me to wait.

rules.rule: asked + question word + subject + verb (tense back).
examples: “Where do you work?” → She asked where I worked.
“Why are you late?” → He asked why I was late.
“Are you coming?” → He asked if I was coming.
She asked whether I liked it.

rules.rule: Requests and orders: ask / tell + person + (not) to + verb.
examples: “Please sit down.” → He asked me to sit down.
“Don’t be late.” → She told us not to be late.

mistakes.wrong: She asked me where do I live.
mistakes.right: She asked me where I lived.

mistakes.wrong: He asked me that am I coming.
mistakes.right: He asked me if I was coming.
She told me not to go.

mistakes.wrong: He asked to me to help.
mistakes.why: ask + person, no “to” before the person.

ex.q: He asked me where was the station.
ex.fixed: He asked me where the station was.

ex.q: She asked me do I like coffee.
ex.fixed: She asked me if I liked coffee.

ex.q: The manager told us don't use our phones.
ex.fixed: The manager told us not to use our phones.

ex.q: He asked me ___ open the window. (request)

ex.a: She asked me why I was so quiet.

ex.q: Report it: My boss asked, “Can you stay late?”
a: My boss asked if I could stay late
My boss asked me if I could stay late
My boss asked whether I could stay late
My boss asked me whether I could stay late
ex.y: My boss asked (me) if I could stay late.

talk: Think of a job interview or a meeting you had. Report three questions they asked you and one thing they asked you to do.
